description: We are comprised of junior cybersecurity enthusiasts from Nasser Center for Science and Technology, and we are interested in research, AI usage, and turning data into a useful visible 3D map. We already have our team decided, but we are still very welcome to receive your support on our hackathon journey.  We're building MarsDelta, a website that works offline so that astronauts can access their own guide on their tablets
summary:
Mars Delta is an offline-capable, data-assisted mars exploration and navigation system designed to detect evolving Martian terrain and support safer, more informed astronaut decisions. 
It plans safe walking routes on real NASA/USGS HiRISE terrain, estimates whether the crew can return with enough oxygen and power, and warns when the ground has changed since the route was planned. 
At Nili Patera, it lines up two HiRISE images taken months apart, detects where dunes and ripples moved, and checks whether a planned walk crosses those areas. At Jezero Crater, it plans a science walk on a 2 m elevation model, checked against real Perseverance Mastcam-Z photos and the rover’s actual path. 
A 3D Mars globe, a crew tablet view, simulated suit-beacon tracking are different views that are simulated in the website. Today’s maps show what Mars looked like at one point in time. However, MarsDelta shows whether that is still true and which matters because one wrong turn on Mars can cost a life.
details:
MarsDelta is a Mars walk planner for astronauts. It plans safe walking routes on real Mars terrain and checks whether the crew can get back to the habitat with enough oxygen and battery. It also warns them when the ground along a route has changed since the maps were made. It covers two real sites: Jezero Crater, where Perseverance is exploring, and the Nili Patera dune field. This tool simulates three views for different contexts: A 3D Mars globe, an astronaut tablet view, and a simulated crew tracking planning system.

What features are included/introduced?

Terrain: We turned a USGS HiRISE elevation model of Jezero into a 2 m grid of height and slope.

Routing: An A* pathfinding algorithm finds the safest path between stops, avoiding steep slopes. It then estimates walking time, climb, and the oxygen and power used. Survival check:

A Monte Carlo simulation runs the walk many times with varied conditions. It reports how likely the crew is to return safely with reserves left.

Change Intelligence: We line up two HiRISE images of Nili Patera taken months apart, matching them on fixed bedrock. We compare their textures to find where dunes and ripples moved, and give each changed area a confidence level. If a planned route crosses one, MarsDelta flags it and suggests a bypass.

Ground truth: The Jezero route is checked against real Perseverance Mastcam-Z photos and the rover’s actual path.

Offline: After the first load the whole app works without internet, because Earth is minutes of signal delay away from Mars.

How will it benefit us?

Safer surface decisions: crews know before they leave whether a walk is survivable. • Up-to-date maps: it shows whether the ground has changed, not just what it once looked like.

Honest data: real NASA data is labeled as real and simulated parts as simulated, with a confidence level on each finding.

Easy to use: a planner for mission control and a simple tablet view for astronauts in the field.

Works offline and in any browser

What do we hope to achieve?

We want to show how future crewed missions can plan walks on Mars using data that changes over time. Exploring safely means knowing whether the ground is still the way the map says. MarsDelta is also a learning tool that lets students and the public explore real Mars terrain and understand its hazards.

Tools, languages, hardware and software:

Web app: TypeScript, HTML and CSS, built with Vite.

Data pipeline: Python with rasterio/GDAL and NumPy, which downloads, aligns and processes HiRISE images, the elevation model and dust data. •

Testing: Vitest unit tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, and 156 automated data-integrity checks.

Hosting: GitHub and GitHub Pages.

Why is our project important?

On Mars there’s no rescue team nearby and no real-time help from Earth. One wrong turn, a steep slope or shifting sand could cost an astronaut their oxygen, materials or even their life. As NASA prepares for crewed missions, tools that turn orbital and rover data into clear, trustworthy walking decisions will be essential. This is what inspired us to create MarsDelta, and to inspire others to explore unknown worlds.
